title: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Compliance Evidence, and Risk Exceptions
author: Daniel Chen
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s security and compliance controls for: RBAC and authentication; audit logging and retention; data residency and retention policies; Secure Software Development Life Cycle (Secure SDLC); incident response security procedures; compliance evidence workflows; and risk & exception handling. It is intended for engineering leads, security reviewers, compliance, and operations teams.

Scope:
- Applies to all production and non-production systems that process customer data, authentication/authorization services, logging infrastructure, and GRC evidence stores.
- Does NOT replace customer-specific contractual requirements; use this as the company baseline and follow contract-specific addenda for regulated customers.

1) RBAC & Authentication

Summary:
Redwood uses role-based access control backed by centralized identity providers and short-lived credentials for all critical systems. The goal is least privilege, auditability, and rapid deprovisioning.

Roles and permissions (examples):
- Platform Admin: full control of infra, deployments, and billing (restrict to < 5 people).
- Security Admin: manage IAM, KMS, audit configuration, and incident response actions.
- SRE: elevated operational permissions (runbooks, restart, scale).
- Developer: CI/CD deploy rights to non-prod and can request production access via approved workflow.
- Read-only: access to dashboards/logs without edit rights.

Authentication mechanisms and policies:
- Single Sign-On (SSO): SAML2 / OIDC via corporate IdP (Okta).
- Multi-factor Authentication (MFA): required for all interactive access, enforced via IdP (hardware token or mobile OTP).
- Service authentication: short-lived mTLS certificates issued by internal PKI or short-lived cloud IAM tokens.
- Privileged access: just-in-time (JIT) elevation via approval flow for access > 1 hour; elevation requires 2 approvers for high-risk actions.
- Key management: customer and platform keys are in KMS (AWS KMS / Cloud HSM) with AES-256 encryption and automated rotation every 90 days for platform keys. Customer-managed keys (CMK) are supported for Private deployments.

Access lifecycle controls:
1. Onboarding: access requests via internal access portal; approval by owner team + security reviewer.
2. Periodic reviews: quarterly privileged access reviews for all Admin/Security roles.
3. Offboarding: user deprovisioning should happen within 1 hour of HR signal/termination.

2) Audit Logging

Objectives:
- Capture authentication, authorization, administrative actions, deployment events, data access, and high-fidelity system telemetry.
- Ensure logs are tamper-evident, retained according to policy, and available for investigation and compliance evidence.

Log sources and pipeline (high level):
- Sources: API gateway, model-serving nodes, control plane, CI/CD, KMS access logs, database audit logs, admin consoles.
- Aggregation: Fluentd/Vector -> central log cluster (Splunk/Datadog Log + Object Storage backup).
- Integrity: write-once object store + HMAC-based ingest signature at collection time.
- Monitoring: alerting rules for anomalous admin actions, privilege escalations, and failed auth spikes.

Retention windows (default):
- Prod auth/admin/audit logs: 365 days (searchable).
- Long-term archive for compliance: 7 years (cold storage, restores on request).
- Non-prod environments: 90 days.

Audit log SLOs and ownership:
- Collection success: >99.9% of logs within 1 minute of generation.
- Alerting: security team to acknowledge critical ingestion failure alerts within 15 minutes.
- Owners: Logging Team (eng-infra) owns pipeline; Security owns alerting rules and retention policy.

Example audit configuration table:
| Source | Retention (searchable) | Archive | Owner |
| API Gateway | 365d | S3 Glacier (7y) | eng-infra |
| KMS Access Logs | 365d | S3 Glacier (7y) | security |
| DB Audit | 365d | S3 Glacier (7y) | eng-platform |

3) Data Residency & Retention

Policy principles:
- Customers may require region-specific residency; Redwood provides region pinning for Hosted and Dedicated offerings.
- Data classification: PII, Customer Confidential, Internal. Retention policies map to classification and contractual terms.

Residency by offering:
- Hosted API: default regional processing based on customer region (US, EU, APAC). For regulated customers, escrowed Private deployments or Dedicated zones are available.
- Dedicated/Private: customer may require on-prem or VPC-only processing; documented in contract.

Default retention windows (baseline):
- Request logs and input text: 30 days by default for product improvement; configurable per contract.
- Embeddings and derived vectors: 365 days unless customer requests deletion.
- Billing and audit records: 7 years.

Data deletion and eDiscovery:
- Deletion requests: tracked via ticketing system. Deletion in prod targets within 48 hours for standard requests.
- eDiscovery for legal requests: security and legal coordinate; preserve-by-hold actions applied to archive buckets.

Encryption and key controls:
- Data at rest: AES-256, platform-managed KMS by default.
- Data in transit: TLS1.2+; strong cipher suites.
- Customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) supported for Private deployments with HSM-backed KMS.

4) Secure SDLC

Objectives:
- Ensure security is integrated into every stage of software delivery from design to production.

Gates and tooling:
- Threat modeling: required for new services handling customer data; review by security and architecture.
- Code review: mandatory for all changes; at least one reviewer outside the primary author team for production changes.
- Static Analysis (SAST): run on every pull request; critical/major findings must be fixed or accepted by security.
- Dependency scanning (SCA): automated alerts for vulnerable dependencies; critical CVEs block merge until mitigated.
- Dynamic analysis (DAST): scheduled scans for public-facing services and before major releases.
- Secrets scanning: pre-commit hooks and CI checks to prevent secret leakage; all secrets stored in Vault.
- Supply chain controls: signed build artifacts, reproducible builds where possible, and attestations for third-party dependencies.

Release controls:
- CI/CD gates: must pass unit tests, integration tests, SAST, SCA, and policy checks to promote to production.
- Canary deployments: default for production rollouts with automated rollback on error rate/latency thresholds.
- Post-deploy checks: automated canary verification and smoke tests for 30 minutes post-deploy.

5) Incident Response (Security)

Purpose:
Provide the runbook for security incidents that affect confidentiality, integrity, or availability of systems and customer data.

Phases and responsibilities:
1. Detection & Triage
   - Sources: IDS/IPS alerts, SIEM detections, customer reports, SRE alerts.
   - Triage owner: on-call Security Incident Responder (SIR).
2. Containment
   - Short-term containment: isolate affected nodes/services, rotate impacted credentials/keys, block malicious IPs.
   - Communication: notify execs, legal, and customer-success if customer data or SLAs impacted.
3. Eradication & Recovery
   - Root cause analysis, remove malicious artifacts, reimage hosts where required, restore from known-good backups.
   - Validate recovery through tests and monitoring.
4. Post-Incident Review & Reporting
   - Produce postmortem within 7 working days (security-focused), include timeline, root cause, impact, and action items.

Notifications and regulatory timelines:
- Data breach notification: follow contractual/regulatory timelines. Baseline: notify affected customers and regulators within 72 hours of confirming a notifiable breach where required by law (GDPR benchmark).
- Public notifications: coordinated by Legal + Communications.

Forensic evidence collection:
- Preserve disk images, process memory snapshots, and collect relevant logs (separate forensic log copy). Avoid altering original evidence.

Escalation matrix (summary):
- Level 1 (SRE/Security on-call) -> Level 2 (Security Leads + Eng Director) -> Level 3 (CISO + CTO + Legal + CEO for high-severity).

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Evidence catalog and ownership:
- Control mapping: map controls to SOC2/ISO27001/GDPR in the Compliance Evidence Catalog (GRC tool: Drata).
- Evidence owners: each control has a named owner (team + individual) responsible for maintaining artifacts.
- Artifacts: runbooks, access review records, audit log extracts, threat models, scan reports, signed policies.

Routine evidence collection process:
1. Automated evidence: CI artifacts, pipeline logs, SAST/SCA reports ingested directly into GRC.
2. Manual evidence: evidence requests routed to owners with SLA to upload within 10 business days.
3. Quarterly control attestations: owners attest control status; exceptions recorded and tracked.

Audit support:
- External auditors: Security and Compliance coordinate; provide a pre-scoped bundle of evidence and a review schedule.
- Evidence retention: follow the retention policy in section 2; 7-year retention for audit artifacts by default.

7) Risk & Exceptions

Exception process:
- Request: team submits exception request form (Confluence template + risk assessment) into the Risk Board.
- Risk assessment: must include likelihood, impact, compensating controls, mitigation plan, owner, and expiration date.
- Approvals: Risk exceptions require sign-off from Security Manager and, for high-risk items, CISO approval.
- Timeboxed: exceptions expire and require re-evaluation at expiry or sooner if risk posture changes.

Compensating controls (examples):
- If production-level access cannot be fully restricted, use session recording, enhanced monitoring, and shortened credential TTLs as compensations.

Risk register and reporting:
- All exceptions added to the corporate Risk Register and reviewed in the monthly Security Risk Review. High/severe exceptions surfaced to the board quarterly.

8) Roles & Ownership (summary)
- Security (owner): policy, incident response, control assessments, control approvals.
- Eng-Infra (owner): logging pipeline, retention enforcement, backup and archive.
- Eng-Platform (owner): deployment gates, SSO integration, key management integration.
- Legal: regulatory notifications, contractual reviews.
- Product/Customer Success: customer communications and contract-specific data residency decisions.

Appendix: Commands, Runbook snippets, and Tables

Sample JIT access CLI example:
```
# Request elevated access for 4 hours
redwood-access request --role=prod-deployer --duration=4h --reason="emergency bugfix"
```

Sample retention config (YAML):
```
audit:
  prod_searchable_days: 365
  archive_years: 7
non_prod_searchable_days: 90
```

Audit pipeline summary table:
| Component | Service | Owner | SLO |
| Fluentd/Collector | eng-infra | eng-infra | 99.9% delivery within 1m |
| Central Log Store | Splunk/Datadog | eng-infra | 99.9% availability |
| Archive | S3 Glacier | eng-infra | Restore within 24h for compliance requests |
